name: state
content:
# Project state

Kept up to date by each task: what was done, important decisions, known gaps.

## p1-page — The 'Tool' page, served at /

Created `public/index.html` (adapted from `.orys/sketch/code/public/index.html`: added `escapeHtml` used on every value interpolated into the rows' `innerHTML` — code, url/title, and the copy button's `data-u` — since the sketch injected `l.url` raw; set the host span via `location.host` in JS instead of a hardcoded string; fixed the ≤640px table layout so the copy button is never clipped). Added `GET /` and `GET /index.html` to `src/app.ts` (reads `public/index.html` once at module load via `readFileSync(new URL('../public/index.html', import.meta.url))`, checked before `POST /api/links`). Did not copy `alt.html` or add a `/_alt` route; `RESERVED_ALIASES` never contained `_alt` so nothing needed removing there. Created `test/page.test.ts`.

Decisions for later tasks:
- The sketch's mobile CSS (`table-layout:fixed` with only `.num` given an explicit width) let the `Short`/`Target` columns claim unbounded width via auto-distribution, pushing the copy button off-screen at narrow widths. Fixed by giving `Short` and `Target` explicit percentage widths (`th.c-short`/`th.c-target`, 30%/42%) alongside the already-fixed `num` and `c-copy` (both px) so all four visible mobile columns sum to a fixed layout that fits.
- Verifying the ≤640px layout with this machine's headless Chrome needed a workaround: `--headless=new --window-size=<w>,<h>` clamps the real layout viewport to a 500px-wide minimum for widths below that (confirmed by probing a `position:fixed;right:0` marker — it isn't visible in the crop below window-size 500, and becomes partially visible exactly in proportion to `500 - requested_width`), even though the output PNG itself is faithfully cropped to the requested size. Screenshots taken by passing a narrow `--window-size` directly are therefore not reliable below 500px wide. Workaround used here: wrap the target page in a local file with an `<iframe>` sized to the real target dimensions (e.g. 375×900) — an iframe's nested browsing context gets its own layout viewport unaffected by the top-level window's 500px floor — screenshot the (≥500px) outer window, then crop to the iframe's placed rectangle. Any later task taking phone-width screenshots on this machine should use the same iframe-wrapper trick rather than passing a sub-500 `--window-size` straight to Chrome.
- Did not manage to drive the page's submit handler end-to-end through headless Chrome to screenshot the red error message, because scripting into the app's iframe from a `file://` wrapper is blocked by cross-origin restrictions (the iframe trick above only works for passive layout/screenshot, not for reaching into the frame to dispatch events). Confirmed instead, via `curl`, that `POST /api/links` with an invalid URL returns `{"error": "..."}`, and the submit handler (reused near-verbatim from the sketch) renders `b.error` into `#msg` with class `msg err` on a non-ok response — this logic is unchanged from the approved sketch.

No known gaps for this task.

## p1-stats — GET /api/links listing with counts

Added the `GET /api/links` route to `src/app.ts`'s `createApp` handler, placed before the `POST /api/links` check is irrelevant (different method) but *before* `handleRedirect` so `/api/links` is never matched as a single-segment code. Route delegates entirely to `listLinks` from `src/store.ts` (counting and ordering happen in SQL) and maps each result to add `shortUrl`. Created `test/stats.test.ts`.

No known gaps for this task.

## p1-setup — Project skeleton, scripts and test runner

Created `package.json` (type: module, engines node>=24, only `typescript`/`@types/node` as dev deps), `tsconfig.json`, extended the existing `.gitignore` with `*.db`/`*.db-journal`/`*.db-wal`, `test/smoke.test.ts`, and `README.md`.

Decision for later tasks: on this Node version, `node --test test/` (directory with a trailing slash as a CLI arg) fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — it gets misparsed as a module path rather than a test-discovery root. `node --test` with no path argument works correctly and auto-discovers everything under `test/`, and `node --test test/<file>.test.ts` (a specific file, no trailing slash) also works fine. The `test` script in `package.json` is `"node --test"` (no path). Later tasks' per-task verify commands that target one file (e.g. `node --test test/store.test.ts`) are unaffected; just don't pass a bare directory with a trailing slash to `node --test`.

No known gaps for this task.

## p1-store — SQLite data layer and short-code generation

Created `src/store.ts` and `test/store.test.ts`. Fixed the two issues the sketch's `store.ts` had: `makeCode` now uses rejection sampling (discards bytes >= 224) instead of `byte % 56`, so all 56 alphabet characters are equally likely; `createLink`'s collision retry now only swallows a genuine unique-constraint failure (checked via `err.code === 'ERR_SQLITE_ERROR'` and `err.message.includes('UNIQUE constraint failed')`) and rethrows anything else.

Decision for later tasks: `node:sqlite` unique-constraint violations surface as a plain `Error` with `code: 'ERR_SQLITE_ERROR'` and a message containing `UNIQUE constraint failed` (not a distinct error class) — use that check, not `instanceof`, if you need to distinguish constraint failures elsewhere.

No known gaps for this task.

## p1-redirect — GET /:code redirect with click recording

Added the redirect route to `src/app.ts`'s `createApp` handler (checked after `POST /api/links`, before the 404 fallback) and `test/redirect.test.ts`.

Decisions for later tasks:
- The route matcher is a single regex (`/^\/[^/]+$/`) applied only to `GET` requests, so `p1-stats`'s `GET /api/links` route must be added and checked *before* this one in the handler (it would otherwise be swallowed as a single-segment path lookup that returns 404 since `api/links` isn't a stored code — actually `/api/links` has an internal `/` so it already fails the single-segment regex and is safe either order, but keep route-order care in mind for any future single-segment GET route).
- `decodeURIComponent` is wrapped in try/catch; a throw (malformed percent-escape) is treated as "not a matching route" and falls through to the normal 404, not a 500.
- `recordClick` is called through a `safeRecordClick` wrapper that catches and `console.error`s any failure; the 302 is always written regardless, so a broken `clicks` table never blocks a redirect.

No known gaps for this task.

## p1-create — HTTP app factory and POST /api/links

Created `src/app.ts` (`createApp`, exported `ALIAS_PATTERN`/`RESERVED_ALIASES` constants, and the `POST /api/links` route), `src/main.ts` (the env-reading entry point), `test/helpers.ts` (`startTestServer`, reused by later endpoint tasks), and `test/create.test.ts`.

Decisions for later tasks:
- `createApp` takes `{ db, baseUrl }` and reads no environment; only `main.ts` touches `process.env`. Later endpoint tasks (`p1-redirect`, `p1-stats`) add routes inside the same `createServer` callback in `src/app.ts`, matched before the existing 404 fallback — check the route order comment at the top of the handler.
- `test/helpers.ts`'s `startTestServer()` works around the chicken-and-egg problem of needing the real port to build `baseUrl` before `createApp` can be constructed with it: it briefly listens a throwaway server on port 0, reads the OS-assigned port, closes it, then immediately creates the real app bound to that same port. There is a theoretical (and in practice unobserved) race if something else grabs the port in that gap; acceptable for local test-only use. Every test gets its own in-memory database and its own server instance, so tests can run with `node --test`'s default concurrency.
- The body-size cap (8 KB) is enforced while streaming, before JSON parsing, so an oversized body always yields 413 regardless of its content.
- The alias-taken race (check-then-insert) is closed by catching the store's unique-constraint error message and converting it to the same 409 as the upfront `resolve` check.

No known gaps for this task.
